summary: Titled mutual, but the Confidential Information definition protects only Valois's information, and the NDA also has an indemnity, perpetual survival for all information and a 24-hour breach-notice duty.

findings.quote: disclosed by or on behalf of Valois to Halyard
findings.why: The agreement is titled mutual, but Confidential Information is defined as only information disclosed by Valois to Halyard, so Halyard's own disclosures are unprotected.
findings.draft_redline: Replace 'disclosed by or on behalf of Valois to Halyard' with 'disclosed by or on behalf of either Party (the Disclosing Party) to the other Party (the Receiving Party)'.
findings.note_to_counterparty: As this is a mutual agreement, we need the definition of Confidential Information to protect information disclosed by either party. We have proposed a small change to achieve that.

findings.quote: each Party undertakes to act in good faith and observe the confidentiality undertakings set forth herein.
findings.why: The operative obligations in clause 2.2 are drafted for a Receiving Party and Disclosing Party that either party can be, which is the mutual structure, once the definition is fixed.

findings.quote: exclusively and strictly to the extent indispensable for the fulfilment of the Authorised Purpose
findings.why: Use is limited to the Authorised Purpose, which is exploratory discussions about a potential strategic commercial partnership.

findings.quote: the Receiving Party can establish by contemporaneous written proof that such information
findings.why: All four carve-outs are present, but each must be proved by 'contemporaneous written proof', which is stricter than the 'written records' or 'reasonable evidence' standard the playbook accepts.
findings.draft_redline: Replace 'by contemporaneous written proof' with 'by written records or other reasonable evidence'.
findings.note_to_counterparty: The four exceptions are fine, but we would prefer the proof standard to be written records or other reasonable evidence, rather than contemporaneous written proof.

findings.quote: the corporate officers, directors, salaried employees, legal counsel, statutory auditors and external technical consultants of a Party or its Affiliates
findings.why: Group members, advisers and auditors are covered on a need-to-know basis with the recipient liable under 2.3, but insurers are not listed as permitted recipients.
findings.draft_redline: Add 'insurers and professional advisers' to the definition of Authorised Representative.
findings.note_to_counterparty: Please could the list of permitted recipients also include insurers and professional advisers, who are bound by confidentiality duties?

findings.quote: notify the Disclosing Party in writing without delay upon receipt of such demand, to the extent legally permissible
findings.why: Compelled disclosure is permitted, notice is qualified by 'to the extent legally permissible', and there is no duty to resist at the Receiving Party's own cost.
findings.fallback_cited: Notice 'where lawful' and cooperation at the Disclosing Party's cost.

findings.quote: a formal certificate of destruction executed by an executive officer within ten (10) Business Days following such demand
findings.why: Return or destruction is within 10 Business Days with officer-signed confirmation, and clause 5.2 permits legally required copies and automated backups that stay confidential.

findings.quote: shall remain the exclusive and unencumbered property of the Disclosing Party and its respective licensors.
findings.why: Confidential Information and IP stay with the Disclosing Party and clause 6.2 grants no licence beyond review for the Authorised Purpose.

findings.quote: made available on an "as is" and "as available" basis, without any express or implied warranty
findings.why: Information is provided as is with no warranty, and there is no Halyard warranty and no fraud exclusion removed.

findings.quote: Neither Party shall communicate to the public, issue press communiqués, make marketing references or publish social media declarations
findings.why: A mutual publicity restriction requires prior written authorisation of the other party.

findings.quote: shall remain in effect for a period of two (2) years, unless terminated earlier by either Party upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice
findings.why: The agreement term is 2 years with 30 days' notice to terminate early, matching the preferred position.

findings.quote: shall continue in full force and effect perpetually and indefinitely with respect to all Confidential Information disclosed hereunder.
findings.why: Confidentiality survives perpetually for all information, not just Trade Secrets, instead of 3 years after expiry or termination.
findings.draft_redline: The obligations of confidentiality shall survive expiry or termination of this Agreement for three (3) years, save that obligations in respect of any Confidential Information that constitutes a Trade Secret shall continue for so long as it remains a Trade Secret.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would like confidentiality to run for three years after the agreement ends, with continuing protection for trade secrets for as long as they remain trade secrets.

findings.quote: The Receiving Party shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless the Disclosing Party, its Affiliates, and their respective directors, officers, employees and agents
findings.why: The clause adds an uncapped indemnity (mutual in form) for any breach, whereas the playbook allows no indemnity and leaves liability to general law.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We do not usually include indemnities in NDAs, as each party's liability for breach is already addressed by general law. We would be grateful if clause 7.1 could be removed.

findings.quote: Neither Party may assign, sub-contract, delegate, transfer or novate any of its rights, benefits or obligations under this Agreement to any third party
findings.why: Mutual restriction on assignment without the other party's prior written consent.

findings.quote: governed by, and construed in accordance with, the laws of England and Wales.
findings.why: English law governs and the courts of England and Wales have exclusive jurisdiction.

findings.quote: abstain from decompiling, reverse engineering, disassembling, translating, synthesising, decoding or modifying any software components
findings.why: Reverse engineering of software and prototypes is prohibited.

findings.quote: Unless expressly provided herein, this Agreement does not confer any enforceable rights or advantages on any third party
findings.why: Entire-agreement clause does not exclude fraud, and third-party enforcement rights are excluded.

findings.quote: shall notify the Disclosing Party immediately, and confirm in writing within twenty-four (24) hours, upon becoming aware of any loss, misappropriation, security compromise
findings.why: The playbook has no rule on breach notification; this clause imposes an immediate duty with written confirmation within 24 hours on the Receiving Party.
findings.draft_redline: The Receiving Party shall notify the Disclosing Party promptly upon becoming aware of any unauthorised use or disclosure of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information and shall take reasonable steps to contain it.
findings.note_to_counterparty: A 24-hour written confirmation deadline may be hard to meet in practice. Could we move to prompt notification instead?
